title: Primary Pelvic Hydatid Cyst in Adolescent Female
case_text:
A 15-year-old girl presented with complaints of suprapubic discomfort and constipation for 2 months. On inspection, a smooth and nonmobile lump was seen in the suprapubic region 4 cm above pubic symphysis. The lower limit was impalpable. On digital rectal examination, a smooth, spherical mass was felt anterolaterally. Complete blood counts, renal, and liver function tests were normal. Ultrasonography revealed a cystic mass suggestive of the left adnexal cyst. Computed tomography (CT) scan showed a large 10 cm x 5 cm x 11 cm cystic lesion in the Pouch of Douglas [Figure 1a and c]. Internal enhancing membranes with cyst within the cyst appearance was seen [Figure 1b]. Since she belonged to an endemic region, hydatid serology (Echinococcus Immunoglobulin G [IgG] antibodies) was done which was positive. IgG is a good marker for the diagnosis with specificity being 98% and sensitivity 25.7%.
Albendazole (10-15 mg/kg/day) was given preoperatively for 28 days. Approaching via Pfannenstiel incision, a 10 cm x 8 cm cystic mass was seen adherent to the uterus anteriorly and rectum posteriorly. All daughter cysts and laminated membranes were removed [Figure 2].
Microscopy showed hooklets, protoscolices, and daughter cysts strongly suggestive of Echinococcus. The diagnosis was confirmed by histopathology.
The postoperative period was uneventful. The patient was discharged on the 6th postoperative day. The patient was prescribed three cycles of albendazole therapy each lasting for 28 days. She is doing well with no signs of recurrence after 1 year.
